Let the network output $\mu(x)$ and $s(x)=\log\sigma^2(x)$. Ignoring a constant, Gaussian negative log likelihood is $L=\tfrac12[e^{-s}(y-\mu)^2+s]$. Its gradients are $\partial L/\partial\mu=e^{-s}(\mu-y)$ and $\partial L/\partial s=\tfrac12[1-e^{-s}(y-\mu)^2]$. [1](https://probml.github.io/pml-book/book2.html)

A large residual increases predicted variance, while the log-variance penalty prevents increasing variance without cost. For residual 2 and variance 1, the variance gradient is -1.5, so gradient descent raises $s$. Predicting log variance enforces positivity after exponentiation; use stable bounds or parameterization to avoid overflow. Validate interval coverage and residual behavior. A single Gaussian captures input-dependent spread but cannot represent two separated likely outcomes at the same input.
